approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two highest-scoring earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current elites with their original accepted strings and scores. The policy fits every selected sequence with equal weight toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps produce the policy that directly samples complete SMILES; chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refill the next batch. A passive uniform-history draw measures the retained score-ordered selector without supplying training examples.
approach.novelty: Add diminishing exposure weights within the selected historical group. Each historical molecule receives a weight inversely proportional to one plus the number of previous fitting batches that used its original identity. Rescale those weights so history keeps exactly the same total share of the loss and current elites keep their existing weights. This shifts influence toward strong historical examples that have been fitted fewer times. The earlier scheduling sibling changed which records trained; this experiment changes the influence of the same selected records. The adaptation siblings tested target normalization, checkpoint restoration and historical-direction protection. None tested cumulative fitting exposure as a loss weight. A chronological weight audit and a comparison with equal-weight gradients on the same policy state will establish whether the redistribution reaches the actual update. Subsequent useful molecules and scores will determine whether it helps search.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-06c043e9d303 gives the same row coefficient to every selected historical original string, regardless of how often that identity has already participated in online fitting. Its three actual summary.json and run.log pairs confirm completed evaluations with macro mean 0.5132724550531974 and population SD 0.001983869060841892. The retained score-ordered replay mechanism raises accepted historical reward but its Curate observation records only 540 distinct session-local historical identities across 2,100 nonterminal replay exposures, 40.78% duplicate raw draws and 41 batches requiring additional sampling. A read-only chronological reconstruction of those same task logs counts an identity once per earlier selected update that executed at least one optimizer step, including its original current-elite admission. Historical exposures have mean prior fitting count 4.465238095238095, median 3 and maximum 26; 1,560 have at least two earlier fitting uses. In 404 of 420 nonterminal historical updates, the selected histories have unequal prior fitting counts. On the exact recorded memberships, inverse-one-plus-count weighting within history, renormalized to preserve the original historical loss share, reduces the loss-weighted prior fitting count from 4.465238095238095 to 3.333001404338429 across all 420 updates and strictly lowers it in all 404 unequal-count opportunities. Its loss-weighted historical accepted reward changes from 0.37650348649074616 to 0.37857065058092704 on that fixed stream. For the 257 exposures with at least ten previous fitting uses, accumulated loss coefficient falls from 25.7 to 13.948815089815009. These are algebraic weighting opportunities on the Parent trajectory, not reconstructed gradients, alternate learning trajectories or proof that repetition caused duplication. Sibling n-0f987622ee3c changed historical membership scheduling and lost utility; n-26e1b62ff971 and n-9297414147d2 improved aspects of fitting while losing paired mean score, and n-49210e3a6c69 changed targets but failed to complete two replicas. The unresolved behavior is repeated equal-weight influence within the already selected strong historical group.
hypothesis: Within the fixed selected historical replay group, weight each original accepted identity inversely to one plus the number of earlier task-local updates that executed at least one optimizer step with that identity selected, and renormalize those weights to preserve the Parent historical loss share; keep current-elite weights, selected membership and fixed augmented targets unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Less repeated-history influence changed learning, reduced duplicate draws and gave uneven endpoint gains.
finding_summary.insights:
Redistributing influence can change search without broadening replay membership. The child replayed 536 distinct session-local historical identities versus the Parent's 540, and its ordinary mean fitting count actually increased. Yet records with at least ten previous fitting uses received total loss coefficient 13.01 instead of 26.50 under equal weighting on the same child stream. This separates reducing repeated influence from selecting less-repeated records. The cost is a smaller effective historical batch: 4.18 rows on average despite five selected rows.

The effect does not establish better protection of every remembered molecule. Historical squared error fell from 85.86 to 84.09 on the child's fixed tensor, but 906 of 2,100 historical row exposures worsened, compared with 834 in the Parent. Both upward and downward likelihood moves occurred, and 489 historical exposures still had positive, unattainable log-probability targets. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, leaving no skipped-fitting interval that demonstrates forgetting. The positive endpoint result is therefore compatible with weaker exploitation, slower progress in some objectives and a better late discovery in one seed.

Chemical coverage also moved unevenly: distinct docking cores increased from 431 to 537 while deco-hop cores decreased from 392 to 372. The molecular assessment shows familiar ring-rich medicinal chemistry, recurring analogue families and unresolved attachment arrangements. It also finds frequent questionable nitrogen chains in one seed, N-hydroxyaminal linkages and missing stereochemical specification. The counter reduced repeated loss influence; it did not resolve those chemical limitations. The open question is whether this endpoint benefit persists while preserving earlier useful progress and coherent chemistry, rather than whether the weighting can alter learning.
finding_summary.results:
The intended weighting reached the real updates. All 405 nonterminal batches with unequal historical fitting counts reduced the weighted prior-use mean and changed gradient direction. Across the 420 historical batches, the same selected records had mean prior fitting count 4.610 with equal weights and 3.356 with the actual weights. Every first backward pass matched the weighted diagnostic exactly, and all 450 updates changed policy parameters. Current loss coefficients, total historical share, accepted targets, original strings and memory rules remained intact. Separately combining group gradients produced small numerical discrepancies in 31 updates; these do not replace the direct agreement between the weighted objective and the real backward pass.

Subsequent raw duplicate draws fell from 40.78% to 36.22%, novel yield rose from 51.81% to 55.90%, and batches needing further sampling fell from 41 to 29. All fifteen tasks completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.513272 to 0.517655, a paired gain of 0.004383. The three seed changes were +0.001516, -0.007474 and +0.019107. Four task means increased, including an almost unchanged near-ceiling docking endpoint; sitagliptin decreased. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.419605 to 0.406769, so the higher final endpoint did not come with faster useful discovery across the budget. Terminal updates are excluded from the generation conclusions.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal chemistry with concentrated analogue families, questionable nitrogen linkages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks and seeds were read: each task has 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2. The complete child and Parent trajectory panels were examined. All 4,350 child optimizer proposals parse with RDKit and have connected SMILES. Digest aromatic-token occurrence rates are 0.946-0.992 and ring-closure occurrence rates are 0.9805-0.9977; these are fractions of proposal strings, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. RDKit readings of the trajectories give median heavy-atom counts of 24, 30, 29, 24 and 24, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3, in the brief task order. The corresponding numbers of distinct nonchiral Murcko cores are 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775, compared with Parent n-06c043e9d303 values of 465, 392, 431, 729 and 737. Thus the output spans many structures, while leading neighborhoods repeatedly decorate a few aromatic amide, aminopyrimidine, cyclic-amine or sulfonamide families. The Parent already had this broad medicinal-chemistry vocabulary; the child changes which families recur, rather than introducing rings or amines to an otherwise deficient vocabulary. Much connectivity looks conventionally makeable, but synthetic plausibility is marked questionable because a whole seed develops nitro-rich acyltriazene and longer nitrogen-chain chemistry, and another leading family contains N-hydroxyaminals. These are material features of the generated output, not just rare malformed strings. Imine stereochemistry, stability and ionization are also unresolved; parseability alone establishes none of them. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0. RDKit finds molecules with unassigned stereocentres in counts of 81, 71, 225, 195 and 274 in task order. Ring formation and structural variety therefore coexist with incomplete stereochemical specification, occasional oversized products and unreliable preservation of favorable attachment arrangements. The descriptions below associate observed chemistry with recorded scores; they do not establish a binding mode, a synthesis route or an unobserved objective-specific scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The typical proposal has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. The digest leaders are compact methoxypyrrole carboxamides whose amide nitrogen bears an aryl group and a benzyl or pyridylmethyl group; a methoxypyridyl-aniline benzamide is another strong family. These supply aromatic surfaces, a carbonyl acceptor, heteroaromatic nitrogen or pyrrole NH, and modest ether or thioether substitution. Conventional amide and aryl connectivity makes these leaders synthetically plausible on inspection. Seed 1 instead favors pyridylmethyl benzamides carrying arylamino or benzyloxy substituents. The low end includes much larger polyaryl amides, ester/ketone-rich structures and elaborate fused or bridged ring systems. Against the Parent, seed 0 moves from an azaindole ester/carboxamide leader at 0.44029418987347235 to the methoxypyrrole tertiary amide at 0.4902347642636414; seed 1 replaces a pyrazole carboxamide leader at 0.4697065314067379 with the pyridylmethyl benzamide family at 0.44742068512417055. Seed 2 moves from pyrrolylmethyl ureas at 0.4675469497082676 to the methoxypyridyl-aniline benzamide at 0.4767312946227961. These changes remain within compact aromatic carbonyl chemistry.
liabilities: Repeated amide-linked aromatic expansion creates very large, flat structures; one cited low-score product has 55 heavy atoms and six aromatic rings.
Several late proposals switch to hydrazides or imidic-acid connectivity, adding chemical-state and stability uncertainty without reaching the leading compact amide scores.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of a compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement is incomplete: successful pyrrole, pyridylmethyl and arylamino arrangements coexist with linker changes and oversized repetitions that sharply lower the recorded score.

The digest leaders explore many nearby halo and methoxy/thioether variants but do not establish a further rewarded scaffold or missing functional group. Alternative attachment arrangements remain the defensible exploration gap; a particular unseen target structure cannot be inferred.
Assigned configurations are absent even in the more elaborate chiral ring products. The leading compact amides are mostly achiral, so no score advantage from adding stereochemistry is demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The best methoxypyrrole amide scores 0.4902347642636414, versus 0.4888902306186987 for its benzyl analogue and 0.4874375036111007 without the aryl fluorine. Replacing methoxy by methylthio in the best structure gives 0.4663257326807468; adding another fluorine to the benzyl-containing leader gives 0.4607206621975761. These close comparisons support sensitivity to heteroatom identity and placement, not a general reward for more halogens or sulfur. The seed-2 arylamino-linked benzamide scores 0.4767312946227961, whereas the cited related phenoxy-linked final molecule scores 0.32687655641442126; the ring composition also changes, so this does not isolate the linker effect. The cited oversized six-aromatic-ring products score 4.579904380381307e-31 and 2.1246665914165835e-28. Their contrast with the compact leaders indicates a severe size/arrangement mismatch, though low-scoring fragments also occur and smaller is not universally better.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings, all four aromatic at the median; the median carbon sp3 fraction is 0.0. Seed 1 supplies every pooled digest leader: an anilino-substituted pyrimidine linked to additional aryl or aza-aryl rings, with extensive chlorine and fluorine substitution. These are recognizable, potentially makeable aromatic medicinal-chemistry frameworks. Seed 2 supplies larger arylsulfonamide/aza-fused-ring structures carrying anilino and benzylidene-imine connections; the final examples have five or six rings and 38-45 heavy atoms. The full seed-0 trajectory reveals a different chemistry hidden by the pooled best list: nitro-substituted acylhydrazones progress to acyltriazenes and extended alternating nitrogen chains. Of its 290 proposals, 238 contain nitro text motifs and 113 contain azo nitrogen links. The seed-0 maximum is an extended nitrogen-chain structure at evaluation 268, score 0.5899850024995834; it is described from the trajectory but its SMILES is not quoted because it is outside the digest citation set. Relative to the Parent, seed 0 leaves fluorinated acylhydrazones with a maximum of 0.6019131056677991 for this less conventionally plausible nitrogen-rich family. Seed 1 changes from thioether/amine-substituted arylpyridines at 0.6039526921879863 to the pyrimidine family at 0.6186220344491388, and seed 2 changes from imine/thiourea chemistry at 0.5974264705882353 to the larger sulfonamide family at 0.6085883514313919.
liabilities: The seed-0 nitro-rich triazene and longer nitrogen-chain series has questionable synthetic and chemical stability; its frequency prevents treating it as an isolated outlier.
The digest charged-string rate of 0.3333 includes nitro formal-charge notation and must not be read as a corresponding fraction of basic or net-cationic molecules.
Halogen-heavy, mostly planar polyaromatics and the larger sulfonamide-imine series create mass, lipophilicity and conformational concerns. The imines do not specify double-bond geometry.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve plausible nitrogen-linker chemistry while retaining the favorable multiaryl/aza-aromatic arrangement: it also emits extended nitrogen chains and imines in the same scored search.

Distinct core and attachment arrangements among the leaders are underrepresented relative to repeated halo decoration. The trajectories demonstrate sensitivity to architecture but do not identify a specific unobserved replacement scaffold.
Nonplanar and configurationally specified analogues are largely absent from the leading aromatic family. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that the observed objective rewards more sp3 carbon.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best four-aromatic-ring aminopyrimidine scores 0.6186220344491388, whereas the compact sulfur-rich heterocycle scores 0.2568799449604403 and a four-aromatic-ring benzylic sulfone scores 0.26617434238528986. A separate large arylsulfone scores 0.31056527590847915, while the final sulfonamides are near 0.60. Thus aromaticity and sulfur oxidation state alone do not explain the gradient; placement of aromatic groups, aza atoms and nitrogen-containing links matters. Adding another fluorine within a cited pyrimidine/diazine family changes 0.6148947065224348 to 0.6133947554925585, and the cited chlorine/bromine alternatives both score 0.6118691990902945. Those comparisons do not support unlimited halogen decoration. Nor do the respectable nitrogen-chain scores establish stable or makeable chemistry: score-bearing motifs and chemical quality visibly diverge in seed 0.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 29 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings. The high-score molecules combine free aliphatic amines with aryl or aza-aryl groups and flexible carbon/ether linkers. Seed 0 favors arylpyridine-linked phenylpiperidine and related larger saturated amine rings. Seed 1 favors a medium-ring tertiary amine tethered to an arylpiperazine bearing a fluorinated fused aza-aromatic group. Seed 2 favors a piperidinylpropoxy-substituted aryl group combined with a haloaryl side chain through amide, hydrazide, oxime or N-hydroxyaminal chemistry. The cyclic-amine frameworks are recognizable medicinal chemistry, although medium-ring preparation is less routine and the N-hydroxyaminals are chemically questionable. The Parent already generated strong arylated cyclic amines and flexible diamines; its seed-2 diamine maximum of 0.9999977262408726 is replaced by an N-hydroxyaminal maximum of 0.999983244459433. Both sit near the recorded score ceiling despite a substantial change in linker chemistry. Ring-amine production is an existing capability, not a missing one.
liabilities: Multiple ionizable amines combined with flexible, halogenated aromatic appendages can complicate ionization, conformation and physicochemical balance; none of those properties is established by the supplied scalar scores.
N-hydroxyaminal, hydrazide and oxime linkers introduce stability or chemical-state questions, while several near-equal scores show that heavier halo substitutions are not automatically useful.
There are 225 proposals with RDKit-detected unassigned stereocentres and no assigned stereocentre tokens in this task.
missing_features: The leading medium-ring amine and N-hydroxyaminal molecules contain unassigned stereocentres; oxime examples also omit geometric specification. The generator does not identify the configurations being proposed.

Chemically well-characterized, configurationally specified versions of the high-scoring N-hydroxyaminal arrangement are not established. Near-ceiling scores give no evidence for an additional required pharmacophore or for a need to add still more basic nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The arylpiperazine/medium-ring amine scores 0.9999855104574086, and two haloaryl N-hydroxyaminal analogues both score 0.999983244459433. By comparison, a sulfonylated piperidine linked to an aromatic amide scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and an N-acylated piperidine carboxamide scores 2.6715842904959654e-05. These low structures retain rings and nitrogens but lack the same accessible aliphatic amine/linker arrangement, supporting an association with free basic amines in an aryl-rich framework. The final small haloaryl hydroxylamine scores only 0.003081102555053772; it lacks the larger amine-linked architecture. In the retained seed-2 framework a hydrazide scores 0.9461023147087682, a tertiary aminoethanol analogue 0.9924975613605506, and an oxime analogue 0.9960716803043389. High score therefore tolerates several linker types and does not demonstrate that the unusual N-hydroxyaminal itself is necessary, stable or experimentally active.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 24 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The leading chemistry repeatedly combines piperazine with arylsulfonamide groups, fused aza-aromatics or benzodioxole rings. Seed 0 ends with methoxy/chlorophenylsulfonyl N-phenylpiperazines; seed 2 explores N-methylpiperazine sulfonamides and joins a quinoline sulfonyl group and a benzodioxole sulfonyl group through opposite piperazine nitrogens. Seed 1 remains more heterogeneous, with a larger heterocyclic amide/sulfonamide among its leaders. Most leading ring and sulfonamide bonds are conventionally plausible. The low end instead includes acyclic azide, acid, sulfamate and small N-hydroxy compounds. Compared with the Parent, seed 0 loses its fused carbonyl heteroaromatic sulfonamide leader at 0.2354681799202668 for the simpler arylsulfonylpiperazine at 0.2125118592516207. Seed 2 changes from an aryl/saturated-diazacycle framework with an N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide at 0.22841141193470538 to the bis-sulfonyl piperazine at 0.2588686674995393. The generator explores many cores, but its stronger molecules repeatedly use a related sulfonamide/piperazine vocabulary.
liabilities: Repeated sulfonylpiperazine elaboration can accumulate mass and polar groups without improving the leading score.
The worst set includes an organic azide and an unusual N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide, illustrating reactive or questionable connectivity outside otherwise ordinary medicinal chemistry.
Unassigned stereochemistry persists elsewhere in the trajectory, even though the principal sulfonamide/piperazine leaders are mostly achiral.
missing_features: Reliable assembly of complementary ring and linker features remains incomplete: the generator finds useful sulfonamide/piperazine combinations but often returns unrelated cores or expands them without preserving the better score.

Alternative attachment topology at comparable molecular size is insufficiently resolved among the leading analogues. More rings, more sulfonyl groups or more basicity are not independently supported fixes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quinoline/benzodioxole bis-sulfonyl piperazine reaches 0.2588686674995393; the smaller quinoline sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184. The more elaborate compound carrying another sulfonylpiperazine branch has 41 heavy atoms and scores 0.2301209791058402, below the 32-heavy-atom leader. A benzodioxole-linked sulfonamide/piperazine scores 0.2229480268629566 and the simple benzodioxole-propyl N-methylpiperazine scores 0.20637741289048106, whereas the final pyrrolylmethylpiperazine scores 0.10826206026353223. These comparisons favor particular aromatic/linker combinations rather than piperazine presence alone. Both nitrogens of the best bis-sulfonyl piperazine are sulfonylated, so interpreting the gradient simply as a reward for stronger basicity would be chemically wrong. The acyclic azide scores 0.0, the N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide 0.007693218186208301 and the thioether diacid 0.02095188685475281. Their absence of the organized ring/linker combinations distinguishes them from the leaders, but the modest leader scores do not reveal a specific missing target substructure.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 24 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings, but their strong examples are chemically heterogeneous. Seed 2 produces a butylaminoacetyl arylsulfonamide, a fluorinated anilide/oxamide and arylsulfonyl imidazolines carrying ester or imidate substitution. Seed 0 favors a guanidino-substituted fused saturated amine and an unusual bicyclic amide; seed 1 supplies a hydroxy aza-aromatic acylthiourea and a cyanophenyl lactam/sulfone. The best examples span 20-26 heavy atoms and one to four rings, using amines, amides, sulfonamides, amidines and sometimes fluorinated aryl groups. These are mostly recognizable functional groups, although several assembled scaffolds and tautomeric states warrant scrutiny. The low end includes long-chain lipid-like products, peptides, overgrown polyaryls and repeatedly acylated nitrogen-rich molecules. Parent leaders included an aminoalcohol pyrazole carboxamide, a fused aza-aromatic benzamide and an acylhydrazone. Seed 2 moves from that hydrazone maximum of 0.2813509436173544 to the aminoacetyl sulfonamide at 0.32609684308650033, while seed 1 moves from the fused aza-aromatic benzamide at 0.30950439639437716 to the acylthiourea at 0.26424211308214746. The child therefore changes the promising families without establishing consistent recovery of their chemistry.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon chains, peptide expansion and repeated acylation produce severe size/polarity extremes associated with near-zero scores.

The aminoacetyl N-acylsulfonamide combines a potentially basic amine with an acidic functional-group class; neutral SMILES alone does not resolve its relevant ionization state. Imidates, imines and acylthioureas also introduce chemical-state or stability considerations.
There are 274 proposals with RDKit-detected unassigned stereocentres, despite no assigned stereocentre tokens.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the observed favorable balance and attachment of aryl, amine and carbonyl/sulfonyl groups is missing from much of the stream; broad functional-group coverage does not translate into consistent assembly of the higher-scoring combinations.

Assigned stereochemistry is absent in the branched anilide/oxamide, guanidino fused-ring structure and other chiral leaders. Their configurations are unspecified, although a stereochemical score benefit is not established.

The disparate moderate-score families do not identify an obligatory unseen scaffold or heterocycle. The evidence supports exploring compact alternative arrangements and functional-group states, not prescribing the named benchmark molecule.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoacetyl arylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033, the fluorinated anilide/oxamide 0.3085499097640706 and the fluorophenyl sulfonyl-imidazoline ester 0.3034617343186778. Within that last family, removing phenyl fluorine gives 0.24905607529893223, and changing the ester carbonyl to an imidate gives 0.2795168707513844. These local comparisons support sensitivity to functional-group identity and placement. The sulfonyl-imidazoline analogue with an ethylamide instead of methyl ester scores 0.20841151065209942. The very large peptide and lipid-like examples score 0.0, and the repeatedly acylated nitrogen-rich example scores 3.540513082254524e-90. However, the compact final urea/carbamate-linked pyrimidinedione also scores only 2.6445959326166367e-17, so limiting size alone cannot recover the successful arrangements. The digest reports a median of 0.0, but raw trajectories contain many tiny positive scores; that displayed median is not evidence that half the molecules scored exactly zero. Late molecules can remain extremely weak despite the existence of chemically distinct moderate-score examples earlier in the same seed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One complete seed contains 238 nitro-containing proposals and 113 proposals with azo nitrogen links among 290 accepted proposals, including extended nitrogen-chain structures. Elsewhere near-ceiling molecules contain N-hydroxyaminal links, while related hydrazide, oxime and ordinary cyclic-amine frameworks also retain high recorded scores. Thus favorable labels can coexist with questionable linkages, and the useful aryl/amine arrangement is not confined to those linkages.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically plausible nitrogen connectivity while carrying useful aryl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs local functional-group coherence and access to conventional alternatives around accepted ring/linker arrangements. It should be able to vary a suspect nitrogen linkage without losing the surrounding structure, then let the observed oracle feedback determine usefulness; parseability or a high label alone cannot establish makeability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading aromatic amides and aminopyrimidines recur as close halo or heteroatom variants, including equal-score chlorine/bromine alternatives and extra-fluorine substitutions with lower scores. Across the supplied tasks, full trajectories contain 372-775 distinct nonchiral Murcko cores, so the limitation is not global core collapse. The strongest examples repeatedly organize amide, sulfonamide or amine connections in a limited set of ways, while many other arrangements remain weak.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies substituents more reliably than it explores and preserves alternative useful attachment arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs access to changes in ring identity, attachment position and linker placement that preserve the useful surrounding size and functional-group balance. Distinct-core counts or halogen substitutions alone are insufficient evidence that this chemical capability has improved; judge the resulting molecules through the same task-agnostic feedback interface.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Very low-score proposals include a 55-heavy-atom polyaryl polyamide, a 61-heavy-atom peptide and a 40-heavy-atom lipid-like structure. In another leading family, a 41-heavy-atom sulfonylpiperazine elaboration scores below its 32-heavy-atom counterpart. Yet small acyclic fragments and compact urea-rich molecules also score poorly, demonstrating that size control must preserve the useful connectivity rather than simply favor smaller products.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control molecular growth while retaining productive combinations of functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs more reliable size-preserving substitutions, local simplifications and controlled extensions around accepted useful structures. Any size constraint or growth preference should remain independent of objective identity and retain room for the larger arrangements that the actual feedback supports.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All task-level digest stereocentre rates are 0.0. Readings of the complete proposal trajectories find 81, 71, 225, 195 and 274 molecules with unassigned stereocentres in the fixed task order. Leading examples include substituted medium-ring amines, N-hydroxyaminals, branched amides and fused saturated rings; imine and oxime examples also omit geometric specification.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits connectivity without specifying the stereochemical and geometric alternatives present in its own molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs a consistent way to represent and explore actual configurational alternatives and chemically appropriate states of generated structures. The trajectories establish missing specification, not a guaranteed score gain from stereochemical enumeration or from changing protonation or tautomer states.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

method_references.title: Thomas, M., O'Boyle, N. M., Bender, A., and de Graaf, C. (2022). Augmented Hill-Climb increases reinforcement learning efficiency for language-based de novo molecule generation. Journal of Cheminformatics 14, 68. Anchor fixed from the catalogue before this external source was located and read.
